decisions.title: Master Agent Execution Backbone - Phase Establishment
decisions.decision: Roadmap phase P17 (Master Agent Execution Backbone) is established. Its objective is to accept a task, prepare an ordered plan, discover authorized agents at runtime, select one deterministically with recorded rationale, execute locally under a controlled security contract, verify the result independently, and preserve auditable evidence. Its scope covers task intake, ordered plan generation, runtime discovery of authorized CLI agents, deterministic agent selection with recorded rationale, controlled local subprocess execution, independent objective verification, auditable task status and evidence, and failure handling and recovery. Dependencies are P2, P3, P4, P5, and P7. The phase is governance-first: the governance foundation is approved now, and the Task Runner itself is NOT approved and remains NOT_STARTED behind GATE-P17-2.
scope: Establishes P17 in the authoritative roadmap (.sps/architecture/SPS2-ROADMAP.md)
Elaborates the phase in sps2/requirements/P17-REQUIREMENTS.json (REQ-P17-01 through REQ-P17-14)
Defines the task-record contract in sps2/schemas/p17-task-record.schema.json
Records the execution security contract as binding on the first implementation
strict_constraints: No Task Runner implementation before GATE-P17-2 passes
No real task execution before GATE-P17-3 passes
No public deployment, no public network exposure, no listening socket
No unrestricted autonomous execution and no approval-gate bypass
No dependency installation; Python standard library only
No modification of P8, P9, or P10 artifacts

decisions.title: Execution Security Contract - Adoption
decisions.decision: The eleven-boundary execution security contract (sps2/requirements/P17-REQUIREMENTS.json, execution_security_contract, SEC-P17-01 through SEC-P17-11) is adopted as binding on the first Task Runner implementation and on every execution it performs: (1) local-only execution with no public server, no public network exposure, and no deployment; (2) only explicitly authorized CLI tools from an explicit allowlist, with availability discovered at runtime by probing and never assumed from documentation; (3) provider compliance - no circumvention of provider limits, account restrictions, or terms, and no automatic account rotation intended to bypass quotas; (4) every execution has a bounded timeout, captured stdout/stderr, a recorded exit status, and an auditable execution record; (5) directory confinement by a tested containment mechanism, not a working-directory setting alone; (6) no API keys, environment secrets, or credentials in task plans, logs, transcripts, or evidence, and no unrestricted credential access; (7) independent objective verification - a successful agent exit code or an agent's own claim is not proof that the task passed; (8) fail-closed behavior for every enumerated failure mode; (9) Python standard library only; (10) no premature autonomy - no unrestricted command execution, no automatic deployment, no bypasses around existing approval gates; (11) auditable evidence with task identifiers, plan, selected agent, selection rationale, execution status, verification result, timestamps, and integrity digests, never secrets.
scope: Binds the first implementation and every execution
Each boundary names its implementing requirement, acceptance criteria, and required evidence
The negative security suite for SEC-P17-01..11 is a prerequisite of GATE-P17-2
strict_constraints: The contract may not be weakened except by a new User decision recorded in a new decision record
An agent exit code of 0 is never, by itself, evidence of task success
Secret values are referenced by location only, never recorded

approval.basis: Explicit User authorization in session, adopting the eleven boundaries stated in the task directive as the execution security contract for the first implementation (local-only execution; authorized executables; provider compliance; process control; directory confinement; credentials; independent verification; fail-closed behavior; no dependency installation; no premature autonomy; evidence with integrity digests and no secrets).

decisions.title: UQ-P17-01 Resolution - Initial Authoritative Executable Allowlist
decisions.decision: The initial authoritative executable allowlist is exactly one entry: ["opencode"], recorded as data in sps2/p17/allowlist.json with purpose "production". Evidence for the recommendation, gathered without invoking any CLI: opencode is the only executable that is both repository-declared (sps2/core/adapters/registry.json, EXPERIMENTAL, detection.cli ["opencode"]) and present in the environment (PATH resolution only). codex is repository-declared but absent; claude and copilot are present but repository-undeclared; generic is a declarative descriptor with no executable. While GATE-P17-4 is OPEN, agents from a production-purpose allowlist are neither probed nor invoked: discovery and execution refuse them with an explicit disabled outcome. Extending the allowlist (adding claude, codex, or any other executable) is a User decision recorded as a new decision record, never an implementation-time choice.
scope: Resolves UQ-P17-01 (previously OPEN) to a single allowlist entry
Basis: explicit User approval of the revised .sps/plan.md, whose approval checklist states that approval of the plan constitutes approval of this line
Does not enable real-agent execution: GATE-P17-4 remains OPEN and the allowlist is not invocable while it is
strict_constraints: Allowlist membership is a security decision, not an engineering default

decisions.title: UQ-P17-02 Resolution - Verification Authority for Slice 1
decisions.decision: For Slice 1, acceptance is verified by OBJECTIVE acceptance commands only, explicitly provided and validated by the task definition. The acceptance command is executed by a structurally separate verifier (sps2/p17/verification.py) in its own subprocess, with its own record; its executable may not be an allowlisted agent executable, so the verifying command cannot be the agent being verified. An INDEPENDENT_AGENT verifier is deferred; it would require a second allowlisted executable and couples to UQ-P17-03. The executing agent's exit code and output are recorded but are never inputs to the verification result.
scope: Resolves UQ-P17-02 (previously OPEN) for Slice 1 only
Basis: explicit User approval of the revised .sps/plan.md, whose approval checklist states that approval of the plan constitutes approval of this line
Whether an independent second agent may verify HIGH or CRITICAL work remains a later User decision
strict_constraints: A successful agent exit code or an agent self-claim is never proof that the task passed
The verification record must carry an explicit independence statement

decisions.title: UQ-P17-03 Resolution - Orchestration Scope for Slice 1

Parallel specialist lanes (skills/sps/SUBAGENT-PLAYBOOK.md), multi-agent fan-out, and concurrent subprocess control are out of scope for Slice 1 and remain a later User decision. Slice 1 tasks execute one selected agent process per run.

strict_constraints: No parallel or concurrent agent execution may be introduced in Slice 1

decisions.title: GATE-P17-2 Approval - Revised Implementation Plan and Slice 1 Implementation
decisions.decision: GATE-P17-2 is APPROVED. The User approved the revised .sps/plan.md (PLAN-P17-001, Revision 2 - the security-review remediation that distinguishes preventive controls from detection/audit controls from guarantees that cannot be provided, disables real-agent execution by default, and defines GATE-P17-4) after security review, and authorizes Slice 1 implementation within the exact boundaries of that plan. Slice 1 is the narrow, test-double-only vertical slice: task intake, strict validation, ordered plan generation and persistence, deterministic selection with recorded rationale, test-double execution under a bounded timeout, independent objective acceptance-command verification, auditable status and evidence with integrity digests, and fail-closed behavior for every defined failure mode. The approved plan's approval-checklist lines are approved with it, which is what resolves UQ-P17-01 through UQ-P17-04 as recorded in D-P17-4 through D-P17-7. This approval authorizes implementation only. It does not authorize real-agent execution, does not enable any gate, and does not mark Slice 1 implemented, verified, or approved as an outcome: IMPLEMENTED != VERIFIED != APPROVED, and each status must be evidenced on its own axis.
